results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 60 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (p01-p04, scene p05-p09, concepts p10-p16, architecture p17, p47, p18-p28, enforcement p29-p34, intake p35-p41, measuring p42-p46, sharing p48-p50, verticals p53, trade-offs p51-p52, failure modes p54, CA view p55-p57, questions p58, conclusion p59-p60). The five unmatched units are the opening callouts, which the spec places outside its paragraph list.
Introduction callout 'WHY THE BUSINESS CARES' (two_ideas): a fixed callout giving two reasons for one point, why the business cares; not a paragraph unit.
Introduction callout 'KEY POINTS' (two_ideas): the house KEY POINTS format is three bullets by design and carries the thesis as the spec's thesis_statement placement requires.

Architecture ¶1 (two_ideas): the spec's controlling idea for p17 is itself one sentence joining the inferred reference architecture with its single-writer rule; the paragraph keeps the provenance subordinate to the design it introduces.
Measuring ¶5 (two_ideas): p46's controlling idea is how the targets were to be reached, people moved and three automation sources; both halves serve that one point.

Every unit traces to a supporting claim through its section: scene and concepts to S1/S6, architecture to S1/S2, enforcement to S3, intake to S4, measuring to S5, sharing and verticals to S6, closing sections to all; the conclusion synthesizes the thesis. No orphan paragraph.

Each table, figure, quotation and case is introduced and interpreted: the inventory table by its totals, the function and policy tables by the consequences paragraph, the component table by the single-writer rule, each public source with what it shows and its limits, Which? and leboncoin with their architectural lessons, the ladder by the demotion paragraph, the consumer table by the event pattern, the metrics table by the two practices, the 0.6% sample by where the gap sat, the targets table by the following paragraph, the share table by the data-protection constraint, and Figures 1-7 by captions tied to the text.

All declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries except the one listed separately: e.g. contrast into p06 ('what had happened outside Tradeyard NL'), problem_solution into concepts ('Ingrid's question can only be answered once...'), sequence into enforcement ('Once the decision service has decided'), contrast into intake ('Detection is only one way violations arrive'), elaboration into measuring ('Metrics are the other output of the decision record'), problem_solution into sharing ('Now Ingrid's question can be answered'), elaboration into verticals ('Figure 7 leaves...'), conclusion_summary into the conclusion. Trade-offs, Failure Modes and Questions open on headings in the book's conventional closing sequence; the Trade-offs table marks 'Veldmark's choice' against the alternatives, and both flow readers found these boundaries clear.

results.quote: The functions also separate the **listing view** from the **actor view**.
results.finding: Declared elaboration is from decisions about items to decisions about actors. The draft instead claims the five functions 'also separate' the two views, a relationship the paragraph never shows (it is about decision targets, not functions), so the link to the preceding list of terms reads as a non sequitur.

results.quote: The functions also separate the **listing view** from the **actor view**.
results.finding: Reader A: 'the opening "also" reads as a non sequitur. I re-read it to find the link.' The listing/actor distinction is clear; its tie to the functions is not.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'I had to re-read it to see how the five functions "separate" these two views.'

results.draft_locus: Architecture ¶2 (subsection 'In practice: what is publicly documented')
results.quote: The table is a reference design, so the public record behind it matters.
results.finding: Reader A: the evidence survey 'breaks that walkthrough... pulls the reader away from the components just listed and then hands them back.' The difficulty comes from the declared placement of p47 directly after the component table (architecture flow rationale), and p17 already lists the same sources, so the reader meets them twice.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'It interrupts the walk through the components, and it partly repeats the opening paragraph of the Architecture section.'

results.quote: Femke's bike was marked sold at 18:10 on Monday 8 March and removed from search at 18:11, yet the next morning's alert digest, assembled at 17:30 from an earlier snapshot, still featured it.
results.finding: Reader A had to re-read to work out that 17:30 was Monday before the sale and the digest went out Tuesday; the clause order makes the times hard to follow.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'A digest "assembled at 17:30" seems to come before the 18:10 sale, and it is not clear on which day it was assembled.'

results.quote: Figure 4's step that warns the **9 counterparties**, the sellers the account had already reached, is the target design, not what happened in March 2027.
results.finding: The number 9 appears for the first time here, from a figure, and Reader A had to reconcile it with the scene's 37 withheld messages; the scene never says the account had already reached sellers.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'The number 9 appears here for the first time... I had to stop and work out that the 37 were blocked messages and the 9 were sellers already reached.'

results.quote: 10. **Badges that outlive the account's integrity.** A verified badge stays on an account after it is taken over, and makes the takeover more effective.
results.finding: Reader A: verified badges are never discussed in the body, so this is new material in a list that otherwise recaps earlier sections. The spec's controlling idea for p54 names this item while no spec paragraph introduces badges, so the gap originates in the spec.
results.corroborated_by: Reader B, item 3: 'Badges and account takeover as a badge problem are never discussed in the body... this one is out of place.'

results.quote: The design did not aim to remove moderators; the review headcount follows the review volume.
results.finding: Reader A: the table just above shows moderators falling from 158 to about 135, so the opening clause first seems to contradict the numbers and is reconciled only on re-reading. Reported by one reader only.

The does_not_know vocabulary is defined at or before use: policy, moderation pipeline, enforcement action and case in the working-terms list; pre- and post-moderation in parentheses; prevalence and overturn rate in the metrics table (earlier mentions are self-explanatory); trusted flaggers at first use; statement of reasons in the scene; DSA Arts. 16, 20, 21, 22 and 24(5) where they are used. Article 17 is first named at the demotion paragraph with enough context (a restriction needing a statement of reasons) and explained in full later; Reader B called this small and understandable. Common Ground, the advice forum and the brands, which both readers found unexplained, are on audience.already_knows.
The opening is a concrete history (keyword filter, review queue, report button) ending in a pointed question; no dictionary definition, sweeping generalization or announcement-only opening.
The conclusion does not merely restate or introduce new claims; it answers the opening question, replays the incident under the design and hands off.

It joins the decision record, acknowledgements, sample and sharing into one answer and states the so-what: one set of data answers a regulator, a wrongly blocked seller and the board, where queues need a new project each.

It repeats the opening question verbatim and replays 7 March: Belgium days later, Poland, Portugal and Motorvane never, versus one decision citing POL-FRAUD-PAYLINK, warned sellers and the hashed phone on Motorvane's block list.

The cold reader predicted the sections in order: scene with the four stacks and the opening question, five functions and policies as data, the pipeline (components, public evidence, two speeds, modes, human review, LLMs), enforcement to every consumer, intake/cases/appeals/statements of reasons, metrics, sharing and verticals, trade-offs/failure modes/CA view/questions; and the evidence (DSA, Meta, Stripe, OLX, Adevinta, two dated public cases, fictional Veldmark). Not naming Which? and leboncoin is consistent with an opening that announces 'two dated public cases'.

Answer names the missing single-writer decision and acknowledged propagation (Ghost Inventory), the EnforcementApplied event applied idempotently and acknowledged, alerts dropping/excluding digests, recommendations evicting, payments holding/freezing per policy, a propagation monitor with 'Enforced' only after the last acknowledgement, and demotion as an Article 17 restriction moved behind the decision service with a decision record and statement of reasons.

Answer rejects the single rule, proposes risk tiers from category risk, seller trust and listing score, gate plus asynchronous path with the book/rental example, time budgets agreed with general managers, edits as new submissions backed by Which? 2024, and a truthful description of the mode backed by the 2015 leboncoin ruling.

Answer lists the shared machinery (decision service and record, enforcement events and monitor, case tooling, evidence store, statement-of-reasons service, rule runtime and lifecycle, registry with local content, base models, hashed lists where lawful), the per-brand side (overlays, vertical detectors, thresholds, local reviewers), the DPO deciding cross-brand signals with purpose, retention and an impact assessment and no raw content, and sampled prevalence of fraudulent listings by brand with trend next to time to action instead of removal counts.
